Draw an external triangle or polygon mesh

Source: R/layers-mesh.R
geom_mesh_3d.Rd

Draw an external triangle or polygon mesh

Usage

geom_mesh_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatMesh3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  vertices = NULL,
  faces = NULL,
  shade = TRUE,
  wireframe = FALSE,
  hidden = "hide",
  subdivide = 0L,
  remesh = NULL,
  decimate = NULL,
  smooth = 0L,
  curvature = FALSE,
  crease = NULL,
  outline = NULL,
  alpha_mode = "face",
  shading = "flat",
  material = NULL,
  hatch = NULL,
  texture = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

vertices, faces

Optional vertex data frame and face index matrix, passed to mesh_3d(). With faces supplied, data may hold the vertices.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

wireframe

Draw original mesh edges with shared edges deduplicated.

hidden

Hidden stroke policy.

subdivide, smooth

Rounds of mesh_subdivide() and iterations of mesh_smooth().

remesh

Target edge length for mesh_remesh(), or TRUE for the mean edge length.

decimate

Target face count or fraction for mesh_decimate().

curvature

Whether to add the computed variables of mesh_curvature(), for use with after_stat().

crease

Crease angle for mesh_normals(); NULL keeps the input's normals.

outline

Feature lines from outline_3d(), or NULL for none.

alpha_mode

How a translucent surface composites. "face" blends every face over what lies behind it, so a surface seen through itself darkens where it folds over. "surface" paints each sheet (a connected set of faces sharing vertices, such as one isosurface level) as one translucent film: other sheets show through it, its own pieces behind its nearer pieces do not. A sheet of several fill colours needs a device with Porter-Duff groups and alpha masks (ragg, cairo_pdf, svg); other devices, pdf() among them, paint it as "face". The raster and hybrid backends keep, per sample, the nearest piece of each sheet and composite the sheets in depth order, with any fill colours; so does the view_3d() viewer. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), stat_parametric_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

shading

"flat" lights and fills each face uniformly; "smooth" interpolates vertex normals and vertex fills across faces. The raster backend and the view_3d() viewer interpolate per sample, perspective correctly. The vector backend draws a triangle whose colour varies along one direction as one linear gradient, with stops that follow the sRGB curve within the option ggplot3d.shading_tolerance (default 2 / 255 in encoded sRGB), and a triangle whose colour stays within that tolerance as one flat polygon. A run of faces that holds a triangle whose colour varies in two directions by more than the tolerance, which no gradient of R graphics can paint, is drawn as one image clipped to the faces' outline, in its place in the drawing order, at the device resolution and at least options(ggplot3d.smooth_dpi) (default 150) dots per inch. options(ggplot3d.smooth_vector = "subdivide") splits such triangles into flat overlapping pieces instead, at most four times (256 pieces per triangle) and not into pieces narrower than a device pixel, so large faces with distant colours show steps. The layers that draw surfaces (stat_isosurface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and others) accept it too.

material

Surface material from material_3d(): ambient, diffuse and specular strengths, shininess, an optional back-side colour and an illustrative style (toon, Gooch, normal colours). NULL reflects ambient and diffuse light fully, with no highlight.

hatch

Hatching from hatch_3d(), or NULL for none.

texture

An image draped over the faces: a texture_3d() object or anything it accepts. Texture coordinates come from the u and v aesthetics when mapped, and otherwise from x and y, spread over the texture's extent (default the range of the layer). stat_parametric_3d() surfaces use their parameters and rgl meshes their texcoords, whose texture file is read when this is NULL. Each face shows the image over its fill; fill = NA shows the image alone. The layers that draw surfaces accept it too.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Data accepts mesh_3d() output, rgl mesh3d objects and projected sf POLYGON Z or TIN Z objects. With shading = "flat" a numeric vertex fill is averaged per face before colour scaling, and every material must be constant within each face. With shading = "smooth" the fill stays per vertex, numeric or given as colours such as fill = I(hex), and each face interpolates its corner colours in linear light; shade = FALSE shows the vertex colours exactly. A discrete fill splits the rows into groups, so group = 1 keeps one mesh.

The mesh parameters run the mesh processing verbs on each mesh of a panel, in transformed position units, in the order subdivide, remesh, decimate, smooth, curvature, crease.

Examples

v <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1), z = c(0, 0, 1, 1))
ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_mesh_3d(vertices = v, faces = matrix(1:4, 1)) + coord_3d()
cube <- expand.grid(x = 0:1, y = 0:1, z = 0:1)
quads <- rbind(c(1, 3, 4, 2), c(5, 6, 8, 7), c(1, 2, 6, 5), c(3, 7, 8, 4),
  c(1, 5, 7, 3), c(2, 4, 8, 6))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_mesh_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = ggplot2::after_stat(mean_curvature)),
    vertices = cube, faces = quads, subdivide = 3, curvature = TRUE) +
  coord_3d()
